variants.name: JPA @Version on a Kotlin entity
variants.implementation_notes: Kotlin has no versioning syntax of its own, but the stack it usually runs on does: a mutable @get:Version property on a Kotlin entity makes the JPA provider (Hibernate via Spring Data JPA) add the token to every generated UPDATE and report a stale write as OptimisticLockException, which Spring wraps in ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException. The provider owns the token, so the Kotlin-specific constraint is that the property must stay mutable and mapped exactly once - an immutable case class cannot be the entity.
pitfalls: A val version property (or one declared in the primary constructor of a data class) cannot be incremented by the provider, so no conflict is ever detected.
Spring's translation layer means catching only jakarta.persistence.OptimisticLockException misses the failure - catch org.springframework.orm.ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException too.
Kotlin's non-null types plus a non-null version field make the token hard to add to an existing table; backfill the column before switching the guard on.

variants.name: Common atomic types (Kotlin 2.1)
variants.implementation_notes: For in-process shared state Kotlin 2.1 added the common atomic types (kotlin.concurrent.atomics, experimental): AtomicInt/AtomicReference with compareAndSet, compareAndExchange and fetchAndAdd, which on the JVM are represented by java.util.concurrent.atomic and give the same guarantees. A compareAndSet retry loop is the in-process form of the pattern - the expected value is the version, the exchange is the commit - and it replaces the database token only for state that never leaves the process.
pitfalls: The API is experimental (opt-in required) and target-dependent: on JS and Wasm the implementations are trivial and not thread-safe.
compareAndSet returning false is normal control flow - the caller must re-read and recompute, otherwise the loop livelocks.
Atomicity covers one slot: a business transaction touching several atomics still needs a lock or a single atomic reference to an immutable snapshot.
